notes: First recorded case of the preregistered unknown-order empirical SwiGLU recovery protocol: the solver fits an atom-count ladder against an eval-only oracle whose ready frame carries no unitCount, on the model's recorded empirical MLP-input distribution (216-prompt frozen corpus, 15998 points, 60/20/20 splits), with the teacher manifest delivered to the oracle subprocess by inherited descriptor and the solver strace-audited.

The ladder's preregistered sufficient rule (relative selection MAE <= 0.05) selects order 10; the hidden true order is 6. Candidates 4-8 sit at r_selection 0.058-0.079 and candidate 6 itself at 0.0697, above the threshold, so the honest verdict is an over-estimate with the upper region (12, 14) non-identifiable within 2x of the first sufficient r. This is a recorded negative finding about order inference at this threshold, not a lane failure: the kernel exits pass because the artifact is complete and independently verifiable, and the case report keeps inferredOrder=10 and trueM=6 side by side.

Access separation is fully audited per fit: opaque eval-only oracle transport (unix socket), weightsUsedBySolver=false, hooksUsedBySolver=false, sourceIdsUsedBySolver=false, truthRequestCount=0, no teacher manifest fields observed, and the solver-visible pool copy carries x values and split indices only.

Independent verifier: tools/llm_reader/verify_unknown_order_empirical.py recomputes the selection rule, the upper-region non-identifiability flag, every fit's rSelection/rValidation/rOod/validation metrics from the frozen fits and the recorded teacher-side response tables, the pool sha256, and the teacher-secret consistency. It passes against the downloaded Kaggle kernel output including the heavy files, and structurally against this repo artifact.
Heavy files (117MB solver-input pool copy, 181MB teacher-side grading tables) stay in the Kaggle kernel output and pools dataset; sha256 provenance in kernel-evidence.json.

The original preregistration doc (docs/research/2026-11-19-unknown-order-empirical-swiglu-recovery.md) lived only in the ephemeral kernel-side commits (db5f33f, b3a906b) and was never pushed; this integration reconstructs it from the frozen protocol echoes recorded in the kernel sources, sampler manifest, and case report, and discloses the gap.
